The word con as a noun has four distinct meanings in English. Each is common enough that you're likely to encounter all of them in everyday life.
Meaning 1: A Reason Against Something / A Disadvantage

This is most often seen in the phrase "pros and cons." A pro is a reason in favor of something, a benefit or advantage. A con is a reason against it, a drawback or downside.

When you're making a decision — say, whether to move to a new city — you might list out everything good about it (the pros) and everything bad or inconvenient about it (the cons). The cons are all the things that make you hesitate or reconsider.

Examples:

  • "One big con of this apartment is that it has no parking."
  • "We sat down and listed all the pros and cons before deciding."
  • "The plan sounds exciting, but the cons outweigh the pros."

You can also use "con" on its own without "pros," whenever you want to highlight a negative aspect of something:

  • "The only con I can think of is the price."

The plural is simply cons: "There are too many cons to this idea."
Meaning 2: A Trick or Fraud Designed to Deceive Someone

This is one of the most vivid and commonly used meanings. A con is a dishonest scheme where someone tricks another person — usually to steal their money, gain their trust under false pretenses, or get something valuable out of them.

The word here is short for "confidence trick" (also called a "confidence game"). The core idea of a con is that the criminal — called the con artist, con man, or con woman — first builds a false sense of trust with the victim, then exploits it.

The person being tricked is often called the mark.

How a typical con works:
The con artist approaches the mark with a story that sounds believable and appealing — perhaps a too-good-to-be-true investment opportunity, a fake prize, or a sob story asking for help. Once the mark is emotionally invested and trusting, the con artist takes their money (or whatever they were after) and disappears.

Common phrases around this meaning:

  • "Running a con" or "pulling a con" = actively executing a deceptive scheme on someone.
  • "Con job" = another word for a con; also used loosely to mean any situation where someone was misled or deceived.
  • "Con artist" = a person who makes a habit of running cons; someone skilled at deception and manipulation.

Examples:

  • "Selling fake gold jewelry to tourists is a classic con."
  • "He realized too late that the whole 'investment opportunity' was a con."
  • "She's a gifted con artist — she had everyone completely fooled."
  • "That whole deal turned out to be a con job."

Note: "Con" in this sense can also be used as a verb ("He conned her out of her savings"), but that's separate from its noun form. As a noun, it always refers to the scheme or trick itself.
Meaning 3: A Convict (A Person in Prison or Previously Imprisoned)

In informal, everyday speech, con is a shortened form of "convict" — a person who has been found guilty of a crime and sentenced to prison.

This meaning is quite common in casual conversation, journalism, and fiction. You won't usually see it in formal legal writing, but you'll encounter it constantly in films, news stories, and everyday speech.

The most common form you'll see is "ex-con" — someone who was previously imprisoned but has since been released.

Examples:

  • "The prison housed over a thousand cons."
  • "He's an ex-con who is trying to turn his life around."
  • "Three cons escaped from the facility last night."
Meaning 4: A Convention (A Large Fan or Enthusiast Gathering)

In informal usage — especially in fan communities — con is a shortened form of "convention." This refers to a large organized event where enthusiasts gather around a shared interest: comic books, science fiction, anime, video games, fantasy, and so on.

This meaning is widely understood, particularly among younger people and pop culture audiences.

Examples:

  • Comic-Con is perhaps the world's most famous con, held in San Diego.
  • "Are you going to the con this weekend?"
  • "I spent all my savings on costumes and merchandise at the con."
  • "She's been cosplaying at cons for years."

Here's a quick way to keep the four meanings straight in your head:

Pros and cons → "con" = a downside, a negative point.
He ran a con on her → "con" = a trick, a fraud, a deception.
He's an ex-con → "con" = a convict, someone who served prison time.
See you at the con! → "con" = a convention, a fan gathering.

The most frequently used meanings in general conversation are the first two. "Pros and cons" is something you'll hear daily in discussions, debates, and decision-making. "A con" as fraud is equally widespread — it appears constantly in news, crime stories, and casual talk. The "convict" meaning is common in informal speech. The "convention" meaning is specific to pop culture and fan contexts but very recognizable.
